_description: Canonical topic -> subject mapping. Every registered topic in concepts/index.json must appear in exactly one section's topics array. Section ids match the filenames under sections/<id>.html. Each section also carries a `color` letter from the seven accent palette (b=blue, y=yellow, p=pink, v=violet, g=green, c=cyan, o=orange) — single source of truth used by index.html section headers + section-jump pills, tags.html detail-panel section-group accents, and mindmap.html node colors. Loaded via scripts/lib/content-model.mjs; exposed as model.sectionOf(topicId). The `description` field is the one-sentence blurb used by scripts/build-section-indexes.mjs when generating sections/<id>.html — keep it short (a single sentence).

sections.title: Logic & Foundations
sections.description: Sets, formal proofs, models, computability, complexity, type theory, and the limits of provability.

sections.title: Algebra & homological
sections.description: Groups, rings, fields, categories, and the homological machinery that connects them — derived categories, group cohomology, Lie algebras, division algebras, quantum groups.

sections.title: Higher categories & toposes
sections.description: Topoi, Grothendieck sites, simplicial sets, ∞-categories and ∞-topoi — the homotopical refinement of structure-preserving language.

sections.title: Analysis
sections.description: Limits, convergence, measure, Banach/Hilbert spaces, operator algebras, harmonic and Sobolev theory.

sections.title: Probability & statistics
sections.description: Measure-theoretic probability, martingales, stochastic calculus, mixing, information theory, statistical inference, and high-dimensional concentration.

sections.title: Geometry & topology
sections.description: From metric spaces and the fundamental group to Riemannian curvature, characteristic classes, the index theorem, and Ricci flow.

sections.title: Number theory
sections.description: Reciprocity laws, p-adic completions, local/global duality, sieves and analytic methods, and the road to class field theory.

sections.title: Modular forms & L-functions
sections.description: Automorphic forms on the upper half-plane, Hecke algebras, L-function continuation, Galois representations, and the automorphic–arithmetic dictionary.

sections.title: Algebraic geometry
sections.description: Projective varieties, schemes, sheaves, moduli spaces, and the arithmetic capstones that tie it all together.

sections.title: Combinatorics & graph theory
sections.description: Spectral and extremal combinatorics, the probabilistic method, matroids, designs, and expanders.

sections.title: Mathematical physics
sections.description: Symplectic mechanics, the Schrödinger equation, general relativity, and the few-body / chaotic dynamics that test classical predictability.
